lead.headline: Trump waives the Russia sanctions law two days before it bites, lifting the threat of 100% tariffs on India
lead.short: Donald Trump signed an executive order on Friday night suspending most of the Russia sanctions law he signed in September, two days before it was due to take effect. The law let him impose 100% tariffs on the five biggest buyers of Russian oil and gas, a list that includes India and China.

why.text: India's exports to the US no longer face a 100% tariff over its Russian oil purchases, though the order lets Washington reverse course later.

more: The order says suspending the provisions is in the US "national interest". Among those waived are 500% tariffs on Russian goods and 100% tariffs on the main facilitators of sanctions evasion. The law also targeted Vladimir Putin, Russian banks and Moscow's "shadow fleet" of tankers.

Russia's envoy Kirill Dmitriev called it "an important and truly historic moment". Democratic congressman Don Beyer called it "Trump's latest surrender to Putin". India has long said its oil purchases follow price and supply security.

Trump also denied limiting Ukraine's Starshield military internet. "It wasn't me and I don't think it was Elon," he said, after Reuters reported the order came from inside the White House. "If I don't stand up to this, who else will?" Volodymyr Zelensky asked EU leaders on Friday.

update.new: Trump suspended the sanctions law that threatened 100% tariffs on buyers of Russian oil, including India.
update.front: A day after Goyal said the trade deal's first phase was final, the 100% tariff threat hanging over India was shelved.

facts.waived: 100% tariffs on top 5 buyers of Russian oil; 500% on Russian goods

seconds.headline: Supreme Court rules that internet access is a fundamental right for everyone, children included, and suggests a 'child mode' for social media
seconds.short: The Supreme Court on Saturday declared access to and use of the internet a fundamental right of every individual, including children, under Articles 21 and 19(1)(a). Justices J.B. Pardiwala and K. Vinod Chandran said children's safety should come from measures such as a "child mode" for social media accounts, not from keeping them offline.

why.text: It makes any law or order that cuts people off the internet, or bans children from it, harder to defend in court.

more: "The safety of our children and their freedom are not at odds with each other. Our children are entitled to both," the bench said. Denying children the internet altogether, it said, would be "as absurd as saying children below a certain age do not have a conscience worth protecting".

The ruling came as the court issued directions to strengthen how platforms detect and remove child sexual abuse material. Restricting children because platforms had failed to remove harmful content, it said, would mistake the victim for the problem.

"For many children, particularly in remote areas, it is often the only source of learning and information," the bench observed. It described the internet as a marketplace of ideas and said the right to free speech includes the right to receive information.

seconds.headline: CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke is detained again and goes before a magistrate, as Delhi Police file 10 FIRs over attacks on protesters
seconds.byline: THE HINDU · TIMES OF INDIA · 17 OCT
seconds.short: Abhijeet Dipke, who founded the Cockroach Janta Party, was due before a special executive magistrate in Delhi on Saturday after police detained him again. AISA leader Neha Bora was released. Police said they had registered at least 10 FIRs over assaults on protesters, after a week of pressure to act against the attackers.

why.text: The police are now booking people who attacked protesters while still detaining the protest's leaders.

more: One FIR, filed at Connaught Place on 13 October over attacks seen in videos online, has led to one arrest, of a man named Gaurav. Four people were arrested at Kamla Market over a video of protesters, including a minor girl, being assaulted and harassed.
In Chennai, a meeting of DMK MPs chaired by M.K. Stalin demanded that Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar be removed and face an inquiry, and called for a return to paper ballots.

At the UN, India rejected special rapporteur Gina Romero's claim that young Indians face retaliation for speaking out. "In which repressive state does a satirical youth party question the government, marches on the capital, and then sits across the table with senior national leaders?" diplomat Anuj Swarup asked.

update.new: Dipke detained again; police file at least 10 FIRs over attacks on protesters; the DMK demands the CEC's removal.
update.front: After a week of pressure online, Delhi Police have registered cases against people accused of beating protesters.

seconds.headline: Masked settlers attack Palestinian olive pickers in the West Bank, injuring 12 including four Americans and a foreign journalist
seconds.short: Dozens of masked Israeli settlers attacked Palestinian farmers near the village of Abu Falah in the occupied West Bank during the olive harvest, setting fire to cars and trees, a BBC team saw. A local official said 12 Palestinians were hurt, four of them dual Palestinian-American citizens. A foreign journalist was also injured.

why.text: The UN says settler attacks in the past two weeks already exceed those of the entire harvest season last year.

more: Majdi Fheed, an American citizen, was hit with nail-studded sticks and needed treatment for deep head wounds, said Yaser AlKam, a council member from nearby Turmus Aya. "Almost 15 Jewish guys started attacking us with guns, with rocks," Fheed said from the back of a car. His elderly mother was also hurt, and three cars were burned.
The US State Department said it was aware of the reports. "We condemn criminal violence by any party in the West Bank and call for investigations, arrests, and convictions," a spokesperson said.
Imm Khaldoun, 73, said she would always return. "This is my land. It's my right."

seconds.headline: Axis Bank's quarterly profit rises 38% to ₹7,003 crore as loans grow 23% and bad loans fall
seconds.short: Axis Bank reported a net profit of ₹7,003 crore for July to September on Saturday, up 38% from ₹5,089 crore a year earlier. Net interest income rose 12% to ₹15,371 crore, with a margin of 3.36%. Loans grew 23% from a year ago and 9% from the previous quarter. The profit missed analysts' estimates.

why.text: Lending is growing by almost a quarter a year while bad loans keep falling, even after the RBI's October rate rise.

more: Gross bad loans fell 30 basis points from a year earlier to 1.16% of the book, and net bad loans to 0.35%. Provisions for the quarter were ₹1,694 crore. Operating profit rose 6% to ₹11,083 crore.
For the half-year, profit rose 30% to ₹14,117 crore and fee income 6% to ₹12,536 crore.

The bank had raised $10.62 billion in FCNR(B) foreign-currency deposits by 30 September and used some of it to cut costlier bulk term deposits, which fell 8.6% in the quarter. "Our focus remains on building a franchise that combines innovation, trust and execution at scale," chief executive Amitabh Chaudhry said.

briefs.text: The former deputy prime minister was brought in at about 7.30pm on Friday and is under observation in the pulmonary department. He was last admitted in May with age-related problems and was awarded the Bharat Ratna in 2024.

stories.headline: The Oregon school gunman was a former pupil who targeted a special needs class, and a teacher wrestled him before a father shot him
stories.short: The 16-year-old who killed three children and a teacher at Silver Rail Elementary in Bend, Oregon, used to be a student there and targeted a special educational needs classroom, police said on Friday. A teacher tackled him and tried to wrestle his shotgun away before a passing father of two pupils ran in and shot him.

why.text: Police say two people who were not officers stopped the attack before it got worse.

more: Police named two of the dead: Rhoam Summer, five, and Meghan Lambert, 25, a teacher whose family said she "always fought for the underdog and those with special needs". The families of an eight-year-old and an 11-year-old asked that their children not yet be named.

The attacker fired as many as 15 rounds in the classroom and was carrying about 44 more shotgun shells, police said. The bystander had been driving past at lunchtime when he saw shooting in the car park.
"To the people who showed courage in the face of such violence, we owe you a debt of gratitude," Bend police chief Mike Krantz said. A 54-year-old teacher and a seven-year-old remain in hospital.

update.new: The attacker was a former pupil who targeted a special needs class; a teacher fought him.

stories.headline: The Nasdaq falls 2.2% as worries grow that debt-laden AI companies cannot repay their loans, and oil jumps 3%
stories.short: Wall Street fell sharply on Friday as AI stocks sold off again. The Nasdaq Composite lost 2.15% to 26,137.85 and the S&P 500 fell 1.1%. Investors fear debt-heavy AI infrastructure companies will not turn a profit before their loans come due, while oil jumped more than 3% on Middle East supply worries.

why.text: Most of the S&P 500's gain this year has come from AI stocks, so doubts about their debts move the whole market.

more: CoreWeave, the data-centre operator backed by Nvidia, fell again after its bonds sold off this week, pushing their yield above 15%. Broadcom dropped and the PHLX chip index fell for an eighth day in a row.

Reuters reported that some existing and prospective Anthropic investors are weighing a lower valuation for its coming IPO. Consumer and producer inflation came in hotter than expected this week, and CNN's Fear & Greed index ended Friday at 18, extreme fear.
"High oil prices tend to weigh on the price/earnings multiple of stocks," said Rob Haworth of U.S. Bank Wealth Management. Tesla, Meta and Procter & Gamble report next week.

update.new: The sell-off reached Wall Street: the Nasdaq fell 2.15% and CoreWeave's bond yields topped 15%.

stories.headline: Real Madrid demand Javier Tebas resign after the La Liga president compares the club's media methods to Goebbels
stories.short: Real Madrid demanded on Friday that Javier Tebas resign as La Liga president and vice-president of the Spanish federation. Tebas had written on X that the club's communication strategy "is reminiscent of the propaganda mechanisms exploited by Goebbels". He said he was comparing techniques, not ideology, and accused the club of intimidation.

why.text: It is the sharpest open break yet between Spain's biggest club and the man who runs its league.

more: "The Real Madrid management conducts an orchestra of spokespeople, and Real Madrid TV leads the charge," Tebas wrote, replying to two El Debate articles critical of him. He said the channel picks the refereeing decisions that suit its case and ignores the rest.

Madrid's five-point statement called the remarks "absolutely intolerable and extremely serious" and said his clarification did not reduce their "deeply offensive, morally repugnant" nature. It accused him of repeated attacks on the club, on Florentino Pérez and on its channel.
The club also said it had asked UEFA to examine Barcelona's payments to former refereeing official José María Enríquez Negreira, and called for an overhaul of refereeing.
